26 of 68 satin shapes sew below readable size at this scale — columns under 1 mm or details under 4 mm. Enlarging helps but does not fully clear it: the smallest shapes regenerate at any size. Remove or simplify the smallest lettering. The artwork carries 7.9 pixels per millimetre at this width, about 8 across the smallest of this lettering, so it is lost in tracing before any stitch: a larger source image carries it, and a design above about 200 mm gives the tracer enough pixels to try.

4 satin shapes sew the gaps between their own strokes closed at 80 mm: Sa440b739 (6.8 x 11.9 mm) has 80% of the space between its strokes narrower than 1.0 mm, the pull compensation (0.3 mm a side) plus a 0.4 mm thread on Pique knit (polo). Connected lettering and marks with spokes do this; the lever is the size. Its tightest tenth of gap clears that at about 200 mm of design width.

29% of satin stitches are under the 1 mm needle minimum (a healthy plan runs about 10%). Thread breaks are likely. 41 of the 67 shapes carrying them have a normal column width that pinches in places, so the size warning does not cover them — widen those waists.

8.4 trims per 1,000 stitches — professional files run 0.1 to 4.1. Each cut is 2-3 seconds of machine time. 78 of 91 are moves between shapes, so merging or removing the smallest is the cheapest thing to try; the other 13 are inside a shape and it will not touch them.
